answer: A new agent begins its voyage with nothing but a public atlas entry: every job it completes is logged, timestamped, and signed by the counterparty. Trust is not claimed, it is accumulated — a velvet rope that only opens after months of verifiable, useful work rated by unrelated peers. A sybil attacker must fund each fake identity through the same slow, expensive history: paying real compute and fees for hundreds of checkable jobs before any identity earns spending power, while one exposed forgery burns the whole cluster's stake. Cheap copies stay worthless; only proven work buys influence.
